body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Mill Hill Lions Club in his or her name.

Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Canal Park. Born in Canal Park in the years after the war, Angela Tanaka spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

articles.title: Lower Millrace Asks Council for Speed Limit Change
articles.deck: The vote came after 23 residents spoke at Sunday’s session.
body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Residents of Lower Millrace said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.
Public works estimates the work will take about 23 weeks once it starts in October. Councilmember Denise Hobart asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $25,000.

Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.

articles.title: Letter: the Lower Millrace Improvement Group Did a Good Job This Summer
body: To the editor: Please keep the tool library in the budget. Many of us on Franklin Court use it every week.

I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the October meeting. To the editor: I have lived on Franklin Court for 15 years, and I want to say what a difference the Lower Millrace Improvement Group has made.
Hal Caruso, Canal Park
